preamble: In 14th-century Old Polish the four inherited nasal vowels merged in quality into a single nasal /ã/ that kept a length contrast. In the 15th century, as vowel length was lost, the short member was fronted to [æ̃~ɛ̃], the source of modern ⟨ę⟩, while the long member was backed to [ɒ̃~ɔ̃] (⟨ą⟩). Old Polish język 'tongue' and węgiel 'coal' thus have ę from short /ã/. The atlas has no open-mid nasal cell, so [ɛ̃] is filed under ẽ.

examples.note: The long nasal /ãː/ went the other way, to ą [ɔ̃].
